note: Draft library entries for Levi's review (coordinator, 2026-11-25). Not served as approved doctrine. Used only as retrieval passages for the model, which must still pass the KJV checks. Each entry rests on at least two KJV passages, quoted from the bundled text.

entries.match: mary|virgin mary|theotokos|worship mary|pray to mary|prayer to mary
entries.view: Scripture honours Mary as the mother of our Lord and blessed among women (Luke 1:42). She is not to be worshipped or prayed to as a mediator: Christ is the one mediator, and worship belongs to God alone (1 Timothy 2:5; Matthew 4:10). Mary herself needed a Saviour (Luke 1:46-47).

verses.text: And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

entries.match: purgatory|purgatorial
entries.view: Scripture does not teach purgatory. Each person dies once and then faces judgment (Hebrews 9:27), and the blood of Christ cleanses from all sin (1 John 1:7). Forgiveness is received by faith in Christ, not earned by suffering after death. Catholic teaching describes purgatory as a final purification; we test that teaching by Scripture and do not accept it.

verses.text: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

entries.match: saint|saints|intercession|intercede|intercessor|pray to the saints|ask the saints
entries.view: Christ alone is the mediator, and He always lives to make intercession for us (1 Timothy 2:5; Hebrews 7:25). Believers who have gone before are honoured as witnesses of faith (Hebrews 12:1), but Scripture does not teach that we pray to saints. Our prayers are offered to God through Christ.

verses.text: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

entries.match: justif|justified|right with god|made right|right standing|faith alone|sola fide|works save
entries.view: We are justified, made right with God, by grace through faith in Christ (Romans 3:28; Ephesians 2:8-9). Good works are the fruit of faith, prepared by God for us to walk in, not the price of salvation (Ephesians 2:10).

verses.text: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

entries.match: sola scriptura|scripture alone|bible alone|final authority|authority of scripture|authority of the bible|tradition
entries.view: Scripture is God-breathed and is the final authority for faith and life (2 Timothy 3:16-17). Church teachers, creeds and traditions are tested by it, as the Bereans searched the Scriptures to test Paul's teaching (Acts 17:11).

verses.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

entries.match: lord'?s supper|communion|the supper|eucharist|mass|bread and wine|wine and bread
entries.view: The Lord's Supper is a remembrance of Christ's death, proclaimed until He comes (1 Corinthians 11:24-26), and a sharing in His body and blood by faith (1 Corinthians 10:16). Christians differ on how Christ is present in the supper. Scripture's language is remembrance and fellowship, and the guide does not claim that the bread and wine change in substance.

verses.text: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.
The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

entries.match: original sin|born sinful|born in sin|sinful nature|inherited sin
entries.view: All people are born in sin and need a Saviour (Psalm 51:5; Romans 5:12). Through the obedience of Christ, many are made righteous and receive life (Romans 5:18-19).

verses.text: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life. For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

entries.match: grace|unmerited|undeserved|favour of god|favor of god
entries.view: Grace is God's undeserved favour, given through Christ and not earned by works (Ephesians 2:8; Romans 11:6). The same grace trains believers to live godly lives (Titus 2:11-12).

verses.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.
For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;

entries.match: hell|judgment|judgement|eternal punishment|lake of fire|everlasting punishment
entries.view: Scripture teaches that judgment is real and that those who reject Christ face the lake of fire (Revelation 20:15; Matthew 25:46). Christians hold different views on the nature of final punishment, and the guide does not settle that question. Judgment belongs to God, and no one should claim to know any particular person's end. The call is to repent and believe (Acts 17:30-31).

verses.text: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.

entries.match: canon|66 books|sixty-six|books of the bible|apocrypha|deuterocanon
entries.view: The Protestant and Evangelical default is the 66-book canon. The books are received as God's inspired Word, because Scripture is God-breathed and the Spirit moved the holy men who wrote it (2 Timothy 3:16; 2 Peter 1:21). Christians differ on the apocryphal books, and the guide does not rank them.

verses.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

entries.match: confession|confess|indulgence|indulgences|priest forgive|absolution
entries.view: Confess your sins to God, who is faithful to forgive through Christ (1 John 1:9), and confess your faults to one another and pray for one another when that is needed (James 5:16). Forgiveness is a gift of God that cannot be bought (Acts 8:20; Ephesians 2:8-9), so the guide does not accept indulgences.

verses.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

entries.topic: The Council of Nicaea and the deity of Christ
entries.match: nicaea|nicene|council of nicaea|deity|divinity of christ|is jesus god|jesus is god|son of god|of one being|arius|arian
entries.view: The Council of Nicaea (AD 325) affirmed what Scripture teaches: the Son is eternal God, of one being with the Father, and not a created being (John 1:1; Colossians 1:15-17). Protestants and Evangelicals accept the teaching of Nicaea where it agrees with Scripture. The full text of the Nicene Creed is not yet in the library; it must be added from a licence-clear source before it is quoted.

verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.

entries.topic: The Holy Spirit is a person
entries.match: holy (?:spirit|ghost)|comforter|is the spirit a person
entries.view: The Holy Spirit is a divine person, fully God, who teaches, guides and can be grieved and lied to (John 14:26; Acts 5:3-4). Scripture names the Spirit with the Father and the Son in the baptismal command (Matthew 28:19).

verses.text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

entries.topic: Jesus is eternal and the Creator
entries.match: eternal|from everlasting|from the beginning|before abraham|created|creator|pre-?exist|firstborn|was there before|always existed|had a beginning
entries.view: Scripture shows that Christ is eternal and that all things were made by Him: His goings forth are from everlasting (Micah 5:2), He existed before Abraham (John 8:58), and by Him all things were created (Colossians 1:16).

verses.text: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.

For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:

entries.topic: Salvation is by grace, not by good works
entries.match: good works|works|earn|heaven|saved|salvation|get to heaven|go to heaven
entries.view: We are saved by grace through faith, not by our own works, and good works are the fruit of salvation, not its price (Ephesians 2:8-9; Ephesians 2:10).

verses.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
Not of works, lest any man should boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

entries.match: return|second coming|come back|coming of|come again|when will jesus|parousia|will jesus come
entries.view: Scripture teaches that Jesus will return bodily and visibly, in the same manner in which He went up (Acts 1:11). The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout (1 Thessalonians 4:16). No one knows the day or the hour (Matthew 24:36).

verses.text: Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

entries.match: resurrect|rose again|rise from the dead|raised|dead rise|empty tomb|risen
entries.view: Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried, and rose again the third day according to the Scriptures (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). The resurrection is the foundation of our faith (1 Corinthians 15:14).

verses.text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

entries.topic: Prayer is made to the Father through the Son, and to Christ
entries.match: pray to jesus|prayer to jesus|worship jesus|pray to the father|who should i pray|pray to god|praying to jesus|pray to christ
entries.view: Scripture gives examples of prayer addressed to the Lord Jesus, as Stephen prayed (Acts 7:59). Jesus taught us to ask the Father in His name, and promised to answer when we ask in His name (John 14:13-14). Prayer is made to God in Christ's name.

verses.text: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it.

entries.topic: Angels serve God and those who inherit salvation
entries.match: \bangels?\b|guardian|ministering spirit
entries.view: Scripture says the angels are ministering spirits sent to serve those who inherit salvation (Hebrews 1:14), and that God gives His angels charge over those who trust Him (Psalms 91:11). Scripture does not say that each person has a personal guardian angel, so we do not teach that.

verses.text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

entries.match: \bfast(?:s|ing|ed)?\b
entries.view: Jesus taught that when His followers fast, it should be done in secret, not to be seen by others (Matthew 6:16-18). He also said that His disciples would fast when the bridegroom is taken from them (Matthew 9:15). Fasting is a discipline of prayer and humility, not a way to obtain blessing.

verses.text: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;
That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.

entries.match: demon|demons|demonic|evil spirit|devil|oppress|possess|deliverance|set free
entries.view: Scripture teaches that believers wrestle against spiritual forces of evil (Ephesians 6:12). Resist the devil and he will flee from you (James 4:7). Jesus gave His disciples authority over the enemy (Luke 10:19). A believer's protection is in Christ and His Word, and any claim about a particular person is to be tested by Scripture and talked over with the pastor.

verses.text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

entries.match: persecut|suffer for|government persecutes|oppress|suffering for the faith|blessed are the persecuted
entries.view: Jesus blesses those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake (Matthew 5:10), and all who live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution (2 Timothy 3:12). Scripture teaches believers to pray for those in authority (1 Timothy 2:1-2) and to keep faithful under pressure.

verses.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.

entries.match: born again|new birth|born of the spirit|regenerat|born from above
entries.view: Jesus said that unless a man is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God (John 3:3). We are born again not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which lives and abides (1 Peter 1:23).

verses.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

entries.match: election|elect|predestin|chosen before|chosen before the foundation|before the foundation of the world
entries.view: Scripture teaches that God chose His people in Christ before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4), and that those whom He predestined He also called and glorified (Romans 8:29-30). The church's view on the details is under review and is not a settled Perazim doctrine.

verses.text: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.
Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

entries.match: millennium|thousand years|thousand-year|1000 years|reign on earth|reign with christ|thousand year
entries.view: Revelation 20 describes those who reign with Christ for a thousand years (Revelation 20:4), and blessed and holy is the one who has part in the first resurrection (Revelation 20:6). The timing and details of this reign are under review, and our view is not a settled Perazim doctrine.

verses.text: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.

entries.topic: The Nicene Creed (381) and the 1662 wording
entries.match: creed|nicene creed|apostles' creed|apostles creed|the creed
entries.view: The Nicene Creed of 381 confesses the Son as "very God of very God, begotten, not made, being of one substance with the Father" (1662 Book of Common Prayer wording, public domain). It agrees with Scripture that the Word was God and that all things were made through Him (John 1:1; John 1:3).

verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

entries.match: inspired|inspiration|reliab|infallib|inerran|bible is true|trustworthy|word of god is true|how do we know the bible
entries.view: All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine (2 Timothy 3:16). Holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost (2 Peter 1:21). The church's formulation of inerrancy is under review and is not a settled Perazim doctrine.

verses.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

entries.match: hebrews|letter to the hebrews|who wrote hebrews|author of hebrews
entries.view: The letter to the Hebrews does not name its author in the text. It is part of the 66-book Scripture we hold, and it teaches that God spoke in His Son (Hebrews 1:1-2). The letter calls itself a word of exhortation (Hebrews 13:22). We do not claim a named author, and the question is not a teaching matter.

verses.text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,
Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words.

entries.match: worry|worrying|worried|anxious|anxiety|take no thought|trust god about money
entries.view: Jesus taught us not to take thought for our lives, what we will eat or drink (Matthew 6:25), and not to worry about tomorrow (Matthew 6:34). Peter tells believers to cast all their care on God, for He cares for us (1 Peter 5:7). Bring every need to God in prayer with thanksgiving (Philippians 4:6).

verses.text: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

entries.match: angry at god|anger at god|angry with god|complain|lament|why did god|why god|forsaken
entries.view: Scripture gives us honest prayer. The psalmist asked how long God would forget him (Psalms 13:1), and Jesus cried, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? (Psalms 22:1; Matthew 27:46). Bring your anger and questions to God in prayer, and talk them through with a pastor who knows you.

verses.text: How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
